- lab-notebook: Session logging, project status tracking, and work history for AI-assisted development. Use this skill at the end of every coding session to write a session log, update project status, and commit changes. Also use when starting a session to orient on a project's current state, when creating a new project entry in the notebook, or when asked to "log this", "update the notebook", "write up what we did", or "what's the status of <project>". Trigger broadly — if the user mentions the notebook, session logs, project status, or next steps tracking, this skill applies.
- python-init: Scaffold a new Python project with modern best practices. Use when the user wants to create a new Python package, library, tool, or application from scratch. Triggers include: "start a new python project", "initialize a python package", "set up a new repo for <something> in python", "create a python project", "scaffold", or any request to create a fresh codebase that will be a Python package. Also use when the user asks about modern Python project structure, pyproject.toml setup, or best practices for packaging. Do NOT use for adding features to an existing project or for non-Python projects.
- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
- superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints
- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# OPLM default training configuration — loaded by oplm.config.load_config.
# These are OPLM's opinionated *production* defaults: μP + Muon, with `lr` as the
# μP base LR (see docs/MUP.md). They intentionally differ from the conservative
# oplm.config.TrainConfig dataclass fallbacks (adamw / lr 1e-4 / match_rms_adamw),
# which back bare TrainConfig() / direct construction. tests/training/test_config.py
# checks every key here is a real TrainConfig field (typo guard), not value-equality.
train:
  # Duration
  max_steps: 50_000
  max_epochs: null

  # Batch
  batch_size: 32
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 1

  # Optimizer — μP + Muon is the default recipe (disable via configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml).
  optimizer: muon             # adamw | muon
  # μP base learning rate. With μP on (the default; model.mup_enable), this value
  # transfers across model width automatically — do NOT retune it per preset/size.
  # Tuned once at mup_base_width=512 (Muon, adjust_lr_fn=original). Only retune if
  # you DISABLE μP (e.g. via configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml), where it is no
  # longer width-correct.
  lr: 0.01
  min_lr: 0.0
  weight_decay: 0.01
  adam_beta1: 0.9
  adam_beta2: 0.98
  adam_eps: 1.0e-8
  # μP + Muon REQUIRES "original" (aspect-ratio-only, ~constant across width so the
  # base LR transfers). "match_rms_adamw" scales like √width and does NOT transfer;
  # build_optimizers raises if it is left on with μP + Muon.
  muon_adjust_lr_fn: original          # match_rms_adamw | original
  muon_momentum: 0.95
  muon_nesterov: true
  muon_ns_steps: 5
  # Empirical repeated-block LR correction for the production scaling ray.
  mup_depth_lr_exponent: 0.0
  mup_depth_reference_layers: 24
  max_grad_norm: 1.0

  # Scheduler
  scheduler: warmup_linear    # warmup_linear | warmup_cosine | wsd_linear | wsd_cosine
  warmup_steps: 5_000
  stable_steps: 0             # WSD plateau length (WSD schedules only)

  # Logging
  log_every: 10
  # Default eval cadence for datasets that omit `every`: {steps: N} | {tokens: N}.
  # Left null so an override replaces it cleanly (a non-null dict would deep-merge
  # and collide on the unit key); null resolves to {steps: 10_000} in the Evaluator.
  eval_every: null
  wandb_project: oplm
  wandb_run_name: null
  wandb_enabled: true

  # Checkpointing
  save_every: 10_000
  save_total_limit: 3
  save_final: true            # write a final checkpoint on completion (skips if last step already saved)
  resume_from: null

  # Infrastructure
  seed: 42
  output_dir: outputs
  mixed_precision: bf16       # bf16 | fp16 | no
  compile: false
  compile_mode: default       # default | reduce-overhead | max-autotune
  compile_dynamic: true   # true | false | null(auto) — torch.compile dynamic flag
  throughput_warmup_steps: 50
  peak_tflops: null   # set device peak (TFLOPs) to log MFU

# OPLM default model configuration (HuggingFace OplmConfig field names).
# Authoritative defaults: loaded by oplm.config.load_config. Any field omitted
# here falls through to the OplmConfig.__init__ default. Derived fields
# (head_dim, intermediate_size, rope_dim, nope_dim) are omitted so they resolve
# from the source dimensions unless explicitly overridden.
model:
  # Core dimensions (~400M parameters)
  vocab_size: 33
  hidden_size: 1024
  num_hidden_layers: 32
  num_attention_heads: 16
  max_position_embeddings: 1024

  # Positional encoding (full RoPE by default: rope_dim resolves to head_dim)
  rope_theta: 10000.0
  nope_dim: 0

  # Normalization
  norm_type: layernorm # layernorm | rmsnorm
  norm_eps: 1.0e-6
  norm_strategy: sandwich # pre | sandwich | hybrid | post_sdpa
  qk_norm: true
  qk_norm_mode: channel # channel (LayerNorm/RMSNorm + 1/sqrt(d) scale) | l2 (L2-normalize + learned per-head scale)
  qk_norm_l2_scale_init: null # l2 mode only; per-head scale init (null -> sqrt(head_dim))
  post_embed_norm: false
  mask_dropout: false # zero <mask> embeddings and rescale by expected/observed mask ratio
  mask_dropout_reference_ratio: 0.12 # expected fraction of real tokens that are <mask> (mask_prob * mask_token_prob)
  residual_scaling: sqrt_num_layers # sqrt_num_layers | none
  residual_gate: none # none | scalar | channel (learnable multiplicative refinement on residual writes)
  residual_gate_init: 1.0 # initial value for residual gate parameters
  attn_output_gate: sigmoid # none | sigmoid | silu (post-SDPA G1 output gate, arXiv:2505.06708)
  value_residual: learnable # none | fixed | learnable (ResFormer value residual, arXiv:2410.17897)
  value_residual_lambda_init: 0.5 # constant lambda (fixed) or init (learnable); layers > 0 only
  init_scale_output_projections: true

  # Feed-forward
  ffn_activation: swiglu # swiglu | geglu (gated, 3 proj) | relu2 (non-gated squared-ReLU, 2 proj)
  ffn_bias: false

  # Dropout
  attention_dropout: 0.0
  hidden_dropout: 0.0

  # Embeddings / head
  tie_word_embeddings: false
  mlm_head_activation: gelu # gelu | silu | relu

  # Canon depthwise convolution (on by default: all four positions, k=7)
  canon_enabled: true
  canon_residual: true # residual Canon updates by default
  canon_positions: [A, B, C, D] # subset of {A, B, C, D}
  canon_kernel_sizes: 7
  canon_activation: none # none | silu | gelu

  # μP (maximal update parametrization) — LR transfer across width, ON by default.
  # train.lr is the μP base LR and transfers across width automatically (no manual
  # retune per size). At this default hidden_size (1024) over mup_base_width (512),
  # m = 2, so μP actively scales init/LR. To DISABLE μP, use the AdamW baseline
  # overlay (configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml) — then train.lr must be retuned.
  # See docs/MUP.md. (The bare OplmConfig() dataclass default is mup_enable=false.)
  mup_enable: true
  mup_base_width: 512 # hidden_size of the proxy/base model where the width multiplier m = 1
  mup_output_mult: 1.0 # tunable O(1) readout (output-logit) multiplier

  # Init / checkpointing
  initializer_range: 0.02
  gradient_checkpointing: false
  # full      -> recompute the entire block on backward (max memory savings, ~+30% compute)
  # selective -> keep matmul/SDPA outputs resident, recompute only cheap ops
  #              (less memory savings, much less extra compute). Inert unless
  #              gradient_checkpointing is true. On multi-GPU + train.compile the
  #              trainer auto-disables DDPOptimizer so SAC isn't collapsed to full
  #              recompute (see docs/TRAIN.md).
  gradient_checkpointing_mode: full # full | selective

def test_mup_cli_overrides_apply() -> None:
    """CLI dotlist overrides reach the μP knobs and the derived multiplier updates."""
    cfg = load_config(
        [
            "--preset",
            "400M",  # hidden_size = 1024
            "model.mup_enable=true",
            "model.mup_base_width=512",
            "model.mup_output_mult=2.0",
        ]
    )
    assert cfg.model.mup_enable is True
    assert cfg.model.mup_base_width == 512
    assert cfg.model.mup_output_mult == 2.0
    assert cfg.model.mup_width_mult() == 2.0  # 1024 / 512


def test_default_run_uses_mup_muon_recipe() -> None:
    """With no overrides the production default is μP + Muon at base LR 0.01."""
    cfg = load_config([])
    assert cfg.train.optimizer == "muon"

μP + Muon is the default, so training at any preset just works — `train.lr` is the
μP base LR (`0.01`), reused unchanged at every size:

```bash
oplm train --preset 1B data.train=/data/uniref50/   # μP + Muon + lr 0.01, by default
```

The defaults live in `configs/train/base.yaml` (`optimizer: muon`,
`muon_adjust_lr_fn: original`, `lr: 0.01`) and `configs/model/base.yaml`
(`mup_enable: true`, `mup_base_width: 512`). With μP on, **`train.lr` is the base
LR** and transfers across width — you do not re-tune it per preset.

**To re-tune the base LR** for a new optimizer or data regime, follow the phased
production workflow in [LR_SWEEP.md](LR_SWEEP.md). It ranks held-out validation
loss, repeats finalists across three seeds, verifies transfer across the preset
ray, and measures the production-batch correction.

**To disable μP** (vanilla ESM-C recipe — AdamW plus the pre-2026 architecture,
e.g. for an ablation), apply the opt-out overlay — note its `lr` is a plain AdamW
LR that must be tuned per size:
===

### μP (maximal update parametrization)

μP makes a learning rate tuned on a small proxy model transfer to much larger
models without re-sweeping at every scale. It is **on by default** for `oplm train`
runs (with `train.optimizer=muon`, `train.muon_adjust_lr_fn=original`,
`train.lr=0.01`), and a no-op at the base width. See [MUP.md](MUP.md) for the full
recipe and the tune-once-reuse-`train.lr` workflow; disable it with
`configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml`.

> **Run defaults vs. dataclass fallbacks.** The `Default` column below (and in the
> Train table) is the **run default** from `configs/*/base.yaml` — what `oplm train`
> loads. Bare Python construction (`OplmConfig()` / `TrainConfig()`) and
> `from_pretrained` use conservative fallbacks instead (`mup_enable=false`,
> `optimizer=adamw`, `lr=1e-4`, `norm_strategy=pre`, `attn_output_gate=none`,
> `value_residual=none`, `canon_enabled=false`), so direct use and existing
> checkpoints are unaffected.

| Override | Type | Default | Valid values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model.mup_enable` | `bool` | `true` | Master switch (run default; dataclass fallback `false`). When `false`, init, forward multipliers, and per-group LRs are identical to non-μP runs. |
| `model.mup_base_width` | `int` | `512` | `hidden_size` of the proxy/base model where `m = hidden_size / mup_base_width` equals 1. The production sweep overrides this fallback/default with its forced 768-wide anchor. Must be `≥ 1`. |
| `model.mup_output_mult` | `float` | `1.0` | Tunable O(1) multiplier on the output logits (applied as `mup_output_mult / m` on the readout matmul path). Must be `> 0`. |

### Derived and validated fields

    # Depth-ray cells insert the layer count and bracket multiplier. The multiplier is not
    # redundant with the effective lr: the coarse grid is 1.6x-spaced, so one candidate's
    # x1.6 cell and the next candidate's x1 cell can land on the same effective lr.
    depth = f"-d{_as_int(params['layers'])}" if "layers" in params else ""

content.content:
**`batch_mult` is ranking metadata only — it is never re-applied to a config.** `bridge` records
each candidate's batch-correction multiplier as `batch_mult` and folds the correction directly
into that candidate's `lr` (`lr = candidate["lr"] * multiplier`); every later phase (`confirm`,
`scale`) carries `batch_mult` forward purely so you can see which batch correction a winner came
from, but reads only `lr`, `output_mult`, and `depth_exponent` back out of a selected candidate.
There is no `train.batch_mult` training-config field, and there must not be one applied by hand
either — the correction is already inside `lr`. Re-applying `batch_mult` on top of that `lr` would
square the correction.

## Production WSD schedule

The sweep and 100k scaling cells select the peak stable learning rate; they do not select the
production cooldown. Production uses:

```text
linear warmup
-> 1–2M stable-LR steps
-> 0.5–1M linear-decay steps
```

Configure `scheduler=wsd_linear`, set `stable_steps` to the plateau length, and set `max_steps`
to warmup plus plateau plus decay. For example:

```yaml
train:
  scheduler: wsd_linear
  lr: 0.01  # illustrative; replace with the confirmed production LR
  min_lr: 0.0
  warmup_steps: 10_000
  stable_steps: 1_500_000
  max_steps: 2_260_000  # 10k warmup + 1.5M stable + 750k decay
```

**Watch out for a zero-decay footgun.** The sweep phases in this document deliberately set
`stable_steps = max_steps - warmup_steps` for every proxy cell — for a *short* proxy run that
convention is fine, since selection only cares about the peak stable LR, not a cooldown. That same
arithmetic is **wrong** for a real production run: it leaves **zero** steps between the end of the
stable plateau and `max_steps`, so a `wsd_linear` schedule trains at peak LR all the way to the
end with no decay at all — silently, since nothing errors. This is not a hypothetical: this
repo's own production job scripts previously shipped with exactly that configuration.
`configs/scaling.yaml` gets this right — `warmup_steps: 5000`, `stable_steps: 85000`,
`max_steps: 100000`, leaving a real 10,000-step (10%) linear-decay tail — and is the reference to
copy the pattern from, not the short-horizon sweep cells.

Preserve optimizer state through the small dataset-mixture change at the stable-to-decay
transition. Do not reset momentum or add a second warmup.

## References

- [SLURM.md](SLURM.md) — the general Slurm job-generation layer this runbook builds on.
- [MUP.md](MUP.md) — OPLM's width-μP parameterization and coordinate-check interpretation.

square the correction.

## Production WSD schedule

The sweep and 100k scaling cells select the peak stable learning rate; they do not select the
production cooldown. Production uses:

```text
linear warmup
-> 1–2M stable-LR steps
-> 0.5–1M linear-decay steps
```

Configure `scheduler=wsd_linear`, set `stable_steps` to the plateau length, and set `max_steps`
to warmup plus plateau plus decay. For example:

```yaml
train:
  scheduler: wsd_linear
  lr: 0.01  # illustrative; replace with the confirmed production LR
  min_lr: 0.0
  warmup_steps: 10_000
  stable_steps: 1_500_000
  max_steps: 2_260_000  # 10k warmup + 1.5M stable + 750k decay
```

**Watch out for a zero-decay footgun.** The sweep phases in this document deliberately set
`stable_steps = max_steps - warmup_steps` for every proxy cell — for a *short* proxy run that
convention is fine, since selection only cares about the peak stable LR, not a cooldown. That same
arithmetic is **wrong** for a real production run: it leaves **zero** steps between the end of the
stable plateau and `max_steps`, so a `wsd_linear` schedule trains at peak LR all the way to the
end with no decay at all — silently, since nothing errors. This is not a hypothetical: this
repo's own production job scripts previously shipped with exactly that configuration.
`configs/scaling.yaml` gets this right — `warmup_steps: 5000`, `stable_steps: 85000`,
`max_steps: 100000`, leaving a real 10,000-step (10%) linear-decay tail — and is the reference to
copy the pattern from, not the short-horizon sweep cells.

Preserve optimizer state through the small dataset-mixture change at the stable-to-decay
transition. Do not reset momentum or add a second warmup.

## References

- [SLURM.md](SLURM.md) — the general Slurm job-generation layer this runbook builds on.
- [MUP.md](MUP.md) — OPLM's width-μP parameterization and coordinate-check interpretation.

   correctness test: with μP, per-module activation RMS must *not grow* with

# μP: Learning-Rate Transfer Across Width

**Maximal Update Parameterization (μP)** lets a learning rate tuned on a small
proxy model transfer to much larger models without re-sweeping at every scale.
Tune `train.lr` **once** at a small proxy width, then reuse the same number at
every larger preset.

μP + Muon is the **default training recipe** (`oplm train` uses it out of the box;
`train.lr` defaults to the μP base LR `0.01`). It is a **no-op at the base width** —
at `hidden_size == mup_base_width`, init, forward multipliers, and per-group LRs
are bit-identical to a non-μP run. The production optimizer for μP is **Muon**;
AdamW is also supported. To turn μP off (and recover the conventional ESM-C
recipe — AdamW plus the pre-2026 architecture), apply
`configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml` (see §1).

Backward-compatibility note: the default lives in the **YAML run-config layer**
(`configs/*/base.yaml`). Bare `OplmConfig()` / `TrainConfig()` construction and
`from_pretrained` stay μP-off (the conservative dataclass fallback), and existing
checkpoints load with whatever `mup_enable` they were saved with.

Related references:

- [TRAIN.md](TRAIN.md) — the general training how-to.
- [CONFIG.md](CONFIG.md#μp-maximal-update-parametrization) — the μP model and training knobs.
- [MODEL_ARCHITECTURE.md](MODEL_ARCHITECTURE.md) — the model itself.

---

## 1. Quick start

μP + Muon is the default, so training at any preset just works — `train.lr` is the
μP base LR (`0.01`), reused unchanged at every size:

```bash
oplm train --preset 1B data.train=/data/uniref50/   # μP + Muon + lr 0.01, by default
```

The defaults live in `configs/train/base.yaml` (`optimizer: muon`,
`muon_adjust_lr_fn: original`, `lr: 0.01`) and `configs/model/base.yaml`
(`mup_enable: true`, `mup_base_width: 512`). With μP on, **`train.lr` is the base
LR** and transfers across width — you do not re-tune it per preset.

**To re-tune the base LR** for a new optimizer or data regime, follow the phased
production workflow in [LR_SWEEP.md](LR_SWEEP.md). It ranks held-out validation
loss, repeats finalists across three seeds, verifies transfer across the preset
===TABLE===

### Multipliers across the presets

For the general `mup_base_width=512` default, `i0 = 1536` and the 50M preset is
the `m = 1` base:

| Preset | `hidden_size` | `intermediate_size` | `m` | `m_ffn` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50M  | 512  | 1536 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| 170M | 768  | 2048 | 1.50 | 1.33 |
| 400M | 1024 | 2816 | 2.00 | 1.83 |
| 800M | 1280 | 3584 | 2.50 | 2.33 |
| 1B   | 1600 | 4352 | 3.12 | 2.83 |
| 3B   | 2048 | 5632 | 4.00 | 3.67 |

`m_ffn ≠ m` because `intermediate_size` rounds to a multiple of 256; using the
true per-matrix fan-in keeps the scaling exact rather than approximating
`down_proj` by `m`.

# OPLM default model configuration (HuggingFace OplmConfig field names).
# Authoritative defaults: loaded by oplm.config.load_config. Any field omitted
# here falls through to the OplmConfig.__init__ default. Derived fields
# (head_dim, intermediate_size, rope_dim, nope_dim) are omitted so they resolve
# from the source dimensions unless explicitly overridden.
model:
  # Core dimensions (~400M parameters)
  vocab_size: 33
  hidden_size: 1024
  num_hidden_layers: 32
  num_attention_heads: 16
  max_position_embeddings: 1024

  # Positional encoding (full RoPE by default: rope_dim resolves to head_dim)
  rope_theta: 10000.0
  nope_dim: 0

  # Normalization
  norm_type: layernorm # layernorm | rmsnorm
  norm_eps: 1.0e-6
  norm_strategy: sandwich # pre | sandwich | hybrid | post_sdpa
  qk_norm: true
  qk_norm_mode: channel # channel (LayerNorm/RMSNorm + 1/sqrt(d) scale) | l2 (L2-normalize + learned per-head scale)
  qk_norm_l2_scale_init: null # l2 mode only; per-head scale init (null -> sqrt(head_dim))
  post_embed_norm: false
  mask_dropout: false # zero <mask> embeddings and rescale by expected/observed mask ratio
  mask_dropout_reference_ratio: 0.12 # expected fraction of real tokens that are <mask> (mask_prob * mask_token_prob)
  residual_scaling: sqrt_num_layers # sqrt_num_layers | none
  residual_gate: none # none | scalar | channel (learnable multiplicative refinement on residual writes)
  residual_gate_init: 1.0 # initial value for residual gate parameters
  attn_output_gate: sigmoid # none | sigmoid | silu (post-SDPA G1 output gate, arXiv:2505.06708)
  value_residual: learnable # none | fixed | learnable (ResFormer value residual, arXiv:2410.17897)
  value_residual_lambda_init: 0.5 # constant lambda (fixed) or init (learnable); layers > 0 only
  init_scale_output_projections: true

  # Feed-forward
  ffn_activation: swiglu # swiglu | geglu (gated, 3 proj) | relu2 (non-gated squared-ReLU, 2 proj)
  ffn_bias: false

  # Dropout
  attention_dropout: 0.0
  hidden_dropout: 0.0

  # Embeddings / head
  tie_word_embeddings: false
  mlm_head_activation: gelu # gelu | silu | relu

  # Canon depthwise convolution (on by default: all four positions, k=7)
  canon_enabled: true
  canon_residual: true # residual Canon updates by default
  canon_positions: [A, B, C, D] # subset of {A, B, C, D}
  canon_kernel_sizes: 7
  canon_activation: none # none | silu | gelu

  # μP (maximal update parametrization) — LR transfer across width, ON by default.
  # train.lr is the μP base LR and transfers across width automatically (no manual
  # retune per size). At this default hidden_size (1024) over mup_base_width (512),

  # overlay (configs/train/vanilla_esm-c.yaml) — then train.lr must be retuned.
  # See docs/MUP.md. (The bare OplmConfig() dataclass default is mup_enable=false.)
  mup_enable: true
  mup_base_width: 512 # hidden_size of the proxy/base model where the width multiplier m = 1
  mup_output_mult: 1.0 # tunable O(1) readout (output-logit) multiplier

  initializer_range: 0.02
  gradient_checkpointing: false
  # full      -> recompute the entire block on backward (max memory savings, ~+30% compute)
  # selective -> keep matmul/SDPA outputs resident, recompute only cheap ops

  #              trainer auto-disables DDPOptimizer so SAC isn't collapsed to full
  #              recompute (see docs/TRAIN.md).
  gradient_checkpointing_mode: full # full | selective

The coord-check is the authoritative test that the μP implementation is correct.
It builds a model at several widths, runs a few optimizer steps on one fixed
batch, and records every `nn.Linear`/`nn.Embedding` output RMS per step.

```bash
# The gate (vary width only, fixed depth):
oplm sweep coord-check --config configs/my-run.yaml \
  --widths 128,256,512,1024 --depth 24 --base-width 512 --optimizer muon

# The control — should fan out / grow with width:
oplm sweep coord-check --config configs/my-run.yaml --no-mup \
  --widths 128,256,512,1024 --depth 24 --base-width 512

# The preset ray (co-scale depth with width; see Caveats):
oplm sweep coord-check --config configs/my-run.yaml \
  --scaling preset_ray --widths 512,768,1024 --base-width 512 --optimizer muon
```

The production gate uses base width 768 and is listed verbatim in
[LR_SWEEP.md](LR_SWEEP.md#parameterization-gates).

Done — but the answer to "just set lr and output multiplier?" turned out to be "not quite": the confirmed winner is only valid together with two other values the sweep pins, so I set all four.

**What the confirm cell actually encodes** (`800M-lr0.0035-om0.5-a0.5-s42`): every sweep run forces `model.mup_base_width=768` (the 170M proxy anchor; `phases.py:193`) and carries a tuned `depth_exponent` (`a0.5` = `train.mup_depth_lr_exponent=0.5`). The production default was anchored at `mup_base_width=512`, and MUP.md explicitly warns not to mix results across the two anchors — with base 512 the width multiplier changes, which shifts init variance, the effective logit scale (`mup_output_mult/m`), and the AdamW-group LRs. So dropping lr=0.0035/om=0.5 onto the old 512 anchor would not reproduce what you validated.

**Changes made** (working tree, not committed):

- `src/oplm/configs/train/base.yaml` — `lr: 0.01 → 0.0035`, `mup_depth_lr_exponent: 0.0 → 0.5` (still a no-op at the 24-layer reference depth, which stays 24)
- `src/oplm/configs/model/base.yaml` — `mup_base_width: 512 → 768`, `mup_output_mult: 1.0 → 0.5`, with a comment noting the four values are one tuned set
- `tests/training/test_config.py` — updated the default-recipe and depth-LR assertions, and added `mup_depth_lr_exponent` to the production-overrides allowlist (it now intentionally diverges from the conservative `TrainConfig` dataclass fallback of 0.0, same mechanism as `lr`/`optimizer`)
- `docs/MUP.md` and `docs/CONFIG.md` — updated the default LR mentions, the anchor paragraph (run default now matches the sweep anchor), the per-preset multiplier table (recomputed for the 768 base, `i0=2048`), and the knob-table defaults

Two things I deliberately left alone: `configs/scaling.yaml` omits the winner values by design (`oplm sweep scale` merges them in when generating jobs), and the dataclass fallbacks (`OplmConfig()`/`TrainConfig()`) stay conservative so existing checkpoints are unaffected.

**Gates**: `ruff check src`, `ruff format --check src`, and `ty check src` all pass; full fast suite is green (1805 passed, plus the fixed parametrized case — the handful of ruff complaints in `tests/` are pre-existing and untouched by this change).

One caveat worth a moment of thought: your sweep base config on the cluster (and `scaling.yaml`) set `residual_gate: channel`, while the packaged model default is `residual_gate: none` — the winner was tuned on the channel-gate architecture. If you intend default `oplm train` runs to reproduce the validated recipe exactly, you may also want `residual_gate: channel` in `model/base.yaml`; say the word and I'll flip it.

message.content: Isn't the depth exponent already covered by the residual scaling (default is set to the sqrt of num_hidden_layers)? Or is the depth exponent in addition to the residual scaling?

content.text: Good question — let me pull up the exact reasoning in the repo's docs before answering, since this was worked out during the depth-sweep hardening.

input.description: Read MUP.md depth-scaling section

content.content:
- **Muon's `original` factor** multiplies per-param LR by `√(max(1, d_out/d_in))`
  — a function of *aspect ratio only*. Aspect ratio is approximately constant
  across presets, so the Muon **base LR is constant across width** (the residual
  error from FFN rounding is validated empirically by the coord-check).

### Owner-by-optimizer

- **Muon mode** (`optimizer=muon`): `q/k/v/o, gate/up/down` → Muon at a constant
  `lr`. Only `lm_head.dense` stays on AdamW and takes `lr/m`; `lm_head.decoder`
  (the readout) also stays on AdamW, at `lr ×1`.
- **AdamW-only mode** (`optimizer=adamw`): hidden matrices take `lr/m_W` (`lr/m`
  for hidden-fan-in matrices, `lr/m_ffn` for `down_proj`); embedding, the readout
  `lm_head.decoder`, norms, and biases stay at `lr` (×1).

### Optional repeated-block depth correction

Width-μP supplies `width_aware_lr`. When model depth also changes, the optional
empirical correction for parameters inside repeated Transformer blocks is:

```text
effective_block_lr(L) = width_aware_lr * (mup_depth_reference_layers / L) ** mup_depth_lr_exponent
```

`mup_depth_reference_layers` defaults to `24`, and
`mup_depth_lr_exponent=0.0` makes the correction a no-op. The correction does
not apply to embeddings, the final stack norm, or the MLM head/readout.

The exponent is a consequence of the residual parameterization, not a free
hyperparameter: with the branch scaling frozen at `1/√L`
(`residual_scaling=sqrt_num_layers`), summing per-block updates of size
`η·(24/L)^e` over `L` blocks gives a total one-step feature update
`∝ η·L^(1/2−e)`, so depth invariance pins `e = 0.5`. (CompleteP's depth-flat
Adam LR belongs to its `1/L` branch multiplier, `α = 1` — a different design;
its exponent does not graft onto a `1/√L` branch.) The production sweep pins
`0.5` and *verifies* it on a fixed-width depth ray rather than sweeping a grid —
sandwich norm post-normalizes each branch before the `1/√L` multiplier and the
learned gate, and Muon is neither Adam nor SGD, so the derivation is checked
empirically; see [LR_SWEEP.md](LR_SWEEP.md#depth-ray-lr-transfer-check).

It's in addition to — and in fact derived *from* — the residual scaling. The two act on different quantities: `residual_scaling=sqrt_num_layers` controls the **forward pass**, while `mup_depth_lr_exponent` controls the **size of optimizer updates**. Neither can do the other's job, and the exponent's value of 0.5 only makes sense *because* the residual scaling is 1/√L.

The intuition, following the derivation in `docs/MUP.md` ("Optional repeated-block depth correction"):

- **Forward:** each block's branch output is multiplied by α = 1/√L before being added to the residual stream. At init the L branch outputs are roughly uncorrelated, so their sum grows like √L, and the 1/√L multiplier cancels it — activations stay O(1) at any depth. That's all residual scaling does.

- **Updates:** take one optimizer step at LR η. All L blocks change at once, and their contributions to the output are *correlated* (they all move in the loss-decreasing direction), so they add roughly linearly, not like √L. The total one-step feature change is ≈ L blocks × η per block × the 1/√L branch multiplier ∝ η·√L. So even with perfect forward-pass depth stability, a *deeper* model takes effectively *larger* steps at the same base LR — which is exactly why the tuned LR wouldn't transfer from the 24-layer proxy to deeper presets.

The depth correction fixes that second problem: each repeated block gets LR η·(24/L)^e, making the total update ∝ η·L^(1/2−e). Depth invariance pins **e = 0.5** — the exponent is a consequence of the 1/√L branch scaling, not an independent knob. (Under a different residual design, e.g. CompleteP's α = 1/L, the required exponent would be different; the two settings come as a matched pair.) Because sandwich norm and Muon complicate the clean theory, the sweep didn't trust the derivation blindly — it pinned 0.5 and *verified* it empirically on the fixed-width depth ray (`docs/LR_SWEEP.md`, depth-ray transfer check), which is what the `a0.5` in your confirm cells reflects.

Two practical notes: the correction is exactly 1.0 at the 24-layer reference depth (the 170M anchor), so it changes nothing on the proxy where the LR was tuned — it only kicks in as `num_hidden_layers` departs from 24 (e.g. the default 32-layer model gets hidden-block LR × (24/32)^0.5 ≈ 0.87). And it applies only to parameters inside repeated blocks — embeddings, the final stack norm, and the MLM head/readout are untouched.

content.content:
load-bearing stability tool for deep models (target depths up to ~80 layers). The
spec uses `sqrt(L)` (owner preference); `sqrt(2L)` is an equally defensible
alternative differing only by `sqrt(2)`, revisitable at scale-up.

**Residual gates** (`residual_gate`, off by default). An optional *learnable*
multiplicative refinement applied on top of the fixed `α`, with a separate gate
for each sublayer write:

```
h = x + α · attn_gate · Attn(Norm(x))
y = h + α · ffn_gate  · FFN(Norm(h))
```

`scalar` adds one parameter per write (shape `(1,)`); `channel` adds a
`(hidden_size,)` vector (per-feature gating). Both are initialized directly to
`residual_gate_init` (default `1.0`, i.e. an identity refinement at init — so a
fresh `channel`/`scalar` model matches the ungated block numerically) and are 1D,
so they land in the no-decay AdamW group (including the auxiliary AdamW under
Muon). `residual_gate="none"` adds no parameters and preserves checkpoint
compatibility. Gates refine the existing `residual_scaling`; they do not replace
`α`. The gate composes with every `norm_strategy` (it multiplies the
post-`Norm₂`/`Norm₄` sublayer output under `sandwich`).

===
| `qk_norm_l2_scale_init` | `None` | `l2` mode per-head scale init; `None` → `√head_dim`; positive if set |
| `post_embed_norm` | `False` | |
| `mask_dropout` | `False` | zero `<mask>` embeddings + rescale by `(1−ref)/(1−obs)`; `input_ids` path only |
| `mask_dropout_reference_ratio` | `0.12` | expected `<mask>` fraction of real tokens (`mask_prob·mask_token_prob`); `0 ≤ ratio < 1` |
| `residual_scaling` | `sqrt_num_layers` | / `none` |
| `residual_gate` | `none` | learnable gate on residual writes: `none`/`scalar`/`channel` |
| `residual_gate_init` | `1.0` | init for gate params; finite |
| `attn_output_gate` | `none` | post-SDPA elementwise output gate: `none`/`sigmoid`/`silu`; adds a `(D,D)` `gate_proj` per layer |
| `value_residual` | `none` | ResFormer value residual: `none`/`fixed`/`learnable`; blends later layers' V toward layer 0's `v₁` |
| `value_residual_lambda_init` | `0.5` | constant λ (`fixed`) or λ init (`learnable`); finite |
| `init_scale_output_projections` | `True` | divide init std of `W_o`,`W_d` by `sqrt(2L)` (GPT-2 style) |

# OPLM default model configuration (HuggingFace OplmConfig field names).

model:
  # Core dimensions (~400M parameters)
  vocab_size: 33
  hidden_size: 1024
  num_hidden_layers: 32
  num_attention_heads: 16
  max_position_embeddings: 1024

  # Positional encoding (full RoPE by default: rope_dim resolves to head_dim)
  rope_theta: 10000.0
  nope_dim: 0

  # Normalization
  norm_type: layernorm # layernorm | rmsnorm
  norm_eps: 1.0e-6
  norm_strategy: sandwich # pre | sandwich | hybrid | post_sdpa

  qk_norm_mode: channel # channel (LayerNorm/RMSNorm + 1/sqrt(d) scale) | l2 (L2-normalize + learned per-head scale)

  residual_gate_init: 1.0 # initial value for residual gate parameters

Set it to `null` (i.e. `None`) — that's also the default, so it's only active if something turned it on. `0` is rejected: the validator in `src/oplm/config.py:232` raises `ValueError("save_every_minutes must be > 0 when set")` for any value ≤ 0.

Concretely:

- The packaged default (`TrainConfig.save_every_minutes: int | None = None`, and nothing in `configs/train/base.yaml` sets it) is already off — a bare run checkpoints only on the `save_every` step cadence. The timer is opt-in; in this repo only `configs/scaling.yaml` enables it (`save_every_minutes: 30`).
- To turn it off where a config has enabled it: `save_every_minutes: null` in YAML, or `train.save_every_minutes=null` as a CLI dotlist override (the config loader parses `null` to `None`).

Also worth knowing: when it *is* set, the timer runs **in addition to** the step cadence, not instead of it — so disabling it never changes your step-based checkpoints, it just removes the extra wall-clock saves (its purpose in `scaling.yaml` is bounding preemption loss on long Slurm runs to ~30 minutes).

291	_VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS = ("steps", "tokens")  # "epochs" deferred — EVAL_HARNESS.md §4.6
292	_SCHEDULE_KEYS = frozenset({*_VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS, "at_start", "at_end"})
293	
294	
295	@dataclass(frozen=True)
296	class ScheduleSpec:
297	    """Parsed, behavior-free eval cadence built from an ``every: {unit: N}`` block.
298	
299	    Carries no behavior so it can live in ``oplm.config`` without importing
300	    ``oplm.eval``. The eval harness turns it into a concrete ``Schedule`` via
301	    ``oplm.eval.schedule.build_schedule``.
302	    """
303	
304	    unit: str  # one of _VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS
305	    n: int  # positive
306	    at_start: bool = False
307	    at_end: bool = True
308	
309	
310	def parse_schedule_block(raw: Any, label: str) -> ScheduleSpec:
311	    """Parse an ``every: {unit: N, at_start?, at_end?}`` mapping into a ScheduleSpec.
312	
313	    Args:
314	        raw: The cadence mapping (a dataset's ``every`` or ``train.eval_every``).
315	        label: Human-readable source used in error messages.
316	
317	    Raises:
318	        ValueError: If ``raw`` is not a mapping, names ``epochs`` (deferred), does not
319	            name exactly one valid unit, has unknown keys, the unit value is not a
320	            positive int, or ``at_start`` / ``at_end`` are not actual bools.
321	    """
322	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
323	        raise ValueError(
324	            f"{label}: cadence must be a mapping like {{steps: N}} or {{tokens: N}}, "
325	            f"got {type(raw).__name__}"
326	        )
327	    if "epochs" in raw:
328	        raise ValueError(
329	            f"{label}: epoch cadence is not yet supported (see docs/EVAL_HARNESS.md "
330	            f"§4.6); use {{steps: N}} or {{tokens: N}}"
331	        )
332	    unknown = [k for k in raw if k not in _SCHEDULE_KEYS]
333	    if unknown:
334	        raise ValueError(f"{label}: unknown keys in cadence block: {sorted(unknown)}")
335	    unit_keys = [k for k in raw if k in _VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS]
336	    if len(unit_keys) != 1:
337	        raise ValueError(
338	            f"{label}: cadence must name exactly one of {list(_VALID_SCHEDULE_UNITS)}, "
339	            f"got {sorted(unit_keys)}"
340	        )
341	    unit = unit_keys[0]
342	    n = raw[unit]
343	    if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n <= 0:
344	        raise ValueError(f"{label}: cadence {unit!r} must be a positive int, got {n!r}")
345	    # The schema says bools; parse them strictly. bool(raw.get(...)) would coerce the
346	    # YAML string "false" to True, silently inverting the flag — validate the type.
347	    at_start = raw.get("at_start", False)
348	    at_end = raw.get("at_end", True)
349	    for flag_name, flag_value in (("at_start", at_start), ("at_end", at_end)):
350	        if not isinstance(flag_value, bool):
351	            raise ValueError(
352	                f"{label}: {flag_name!r} must be a bool, got {flag_value!r} "
353	                f"({type(flag_value).__name__})"
354	            )
355	    return ScheduleSpec(unit=unit, n=n, at_start=at_start, at_end=at_end)

421	            raise ValueError(f"mask_token_prob must be in [0, 1], got {self.mask_token_prob}")
422	        if not 0.0 <= self.random_token_prob <= 1.0:
423	            raise ValueError(f"random_token_prob must be in [0, 1], got {self.random_token_prob}")
424	        # The remainder (1 - mask_token_prob - random_token_prob) keeps the
425	        # original token, so the two probabilities must not exceed 1 together.
426	        if self.mask_token_prob + self.random_token_prob > 1.0 + 1e-9:
427	            raise ValueError(
428	                "mask_token_prob + random_token_prob must be <= 1, got "
429	                f"{self.mask_token_prob} + {self.random_token_prob} = "
430	                f"{self.mask_token_prob + self.random_token_prob}"
431	            )
432	
433	
434	@dataclass
435	class OplmConfig:
436	    """Root configuration composing model, training, and data configs."""
437	
438	    # Resolved into oplm.model.OplmConfig (the HF PretrainedConfig) by
439	    # load_config. Untyped so OmegaConf can carry arbitrary HF field keys,
440	    # mirroring how DataConfig.train/.eval are Any.
441	    model: Any = field(default_factory=dict)
442	    train: TrainConfig = field(default_factory=TrainConfig)
443	    data: DataConfig = field(default_factory=DataConfig)
444	
445	
446	def validate_parallelism_compat(cfg: OplmConfig) -> None:
447	    """Reject cross-section config combinations that would deadlock under HSDP.
448	
449	    ``TrainConfig.__post_init__`` validates everything inside ``train.*``; this covers the
450	    one incompatibility that spans sections, so it needs both ``cfg.train`` and
451	    ``cfg.data``. Called from :func:`load_config` (so a CLI/YAML mistake fails at parse
452	    time) and again at the top of ``Trainer.__init__`` (so a directly-constructed config --
453	    tests, sweeps, notebooks -- cannot bypass it). Idempotent and pure; no collectives, and
454	    its inputs are rank-identical, so every rank raises identically.
455	
456	    **Eval under HSDP deadlocks.** ``fully_shard`` mutates the module in place, so
457	    ``accelerator.unwrap_model`` hands the evaluator the ``FSDPModule`` itself, and every
458	    eval forward all-gathers sharded parameters. The eval tasks stripe their work across
459	    ranks (``[rank::world_size]``), so ranks run *different numbers* of forwards -- the
460	    ranks that finish early never issue the matching all-gathers and the group wedges until
461	    ``dist_timeout_minutes``, then crash-loops through the requeue. Making eval
462	    HSDP-safe (rank-padded forward counts, or gathering the model once into an unsharded
463	    eval copy) is follow-up work; until then this refuses the combination up front rather
464	    than letting a multi-node run hang at its first eval.
465	
466	    Args:
467	        cfg: The fully resolved root config.
468	
469	    Raises:
470	        ValueError: ``train.parallelism="hsdp"`` with any eval dataset configured.
471	    """
472	    if cfg.train.parallelism == "hsdp" and cfg.data.eval is not None:
473	        raise ValueError(
474	            "train.parallelism='hsdp' is incompatible with configured eval datasets "
475	            "(data.eval): eval tasks stripe their forwards across ranks, but under FSDP2 "
476	            "every forward all-gathers sharded parameters -- ranks with fewer forwards "
477	            "stop issuing all-gathers and the whole group hangs until dist_timeout_minutes. "
478	            "Run eval as a separate ddp job against the checkpoint, or set "
479	            "train.parallelism='ddp'. See oplm.training.parallel for the limitation and "
480	            "the planned fix."
481	        )
482	
483	
484	def get_preset_config(preset: str) -> DictConfig:
485	    """Load a model size preset by name.
486	
487	    Args:
488	        preset: One of ``"50M"``, ``"170M"``, ``"400M"``, ``"800M"``, ``"1B"``, ``"3B"``,
489	            ``"6B"``, ``"12B"``.
490	
491	    Returns:
492	        DictConfig loaded from the preset YAML.
493	
494	    Raises:
495	        ValueError: If the preset name is not recognized.
496	    """
497	    if preset not in AVAILABLE_PRESETS:
498	        raise ValueError(
499	            f"Unknown preset {preset!r}. Available presets: {', '.join(AVAILABLE_PRESETS)}"
500	        )
501	    preset_dir = files("oplm.configs.model.presets")
502	    yaml_text = preset_dir.joinpath(f"{preset}.yaml").read_text()
503	    return cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.create(yaml_text))
504	
505	
506	# Per-concern default layers, merged at the config root in this order. Each
507	# file is section-wrapped (top-level `model:` / `train:` / `data:`).
508	_BASE_CONFIG_LAYERS = (
509	    ("oplm.configs.model", "base.yaml"),
510	    ("oplm.configs.train", "base.yaml"),
511	    ("oplm.configs.data", "base.yaml"),
512	)
513	
514	
515	def _load_packaged_yaml(package: str, filename: str) -> DictConfig:
516	    """Load a YAML resource shipped inside the package as a DictConfig."""
517	    text = files(package).joinpath(filename).read_text()
518	    return cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.create(text))
519	
520	
521	_NESTED_VALUE_MISSING = object()
522	
523	
524	def _lookup_nested_mapping_value(mapping: Any, path: tuple[str, ...]) -> Any:
525	    """Return a nested mapping value or a sentinel when the path is absent."""
526	    current = mapping
527	    for key in path:
528	        if not isinstance(current, dict) or key not in current:
529	            return _NESTED_VALUE_MISSING
530	        current = current[key]
531	    return current
532	
533	
534	def _reject_removed_sequence_length_alias(override_dicts: list[Any]) -> None:
535	    """Reject removed sequence-length overrides before merging them into the config."""
536	    has_removed_alias = any(
537	        _lookup_nested_mapping_value(ov, ("data", "max_length")) is not _NESTED_VALUE_MISSING
538	        for ov in override_dicts
539	    )
540	    if has_removed_alias:
541	        raise ValueError(
542	            "`data.max_length` has been removed. Use `model.max_position_embeddings` "
543	            "as the sequence-length setting."
544	        )
545	
546	
547	def _reject_unknown_model_keys(model_dict: dict[str, Any], model_config_cls: type) -> None:
548	    """Raise on `model.*` keys that no `OplmConfig` field or HF metadata accepts.
549	
550	    `PretrainedConfig.__init__` silently absorbs unknown `**kwargs`, so a typo
551	    like `model.cannon_enabled=true` would otherwise be retained while the real
552	    `canon_enabled` stays at its default — silently disabling an ablation. The
553	    allowed set is the constructor signature plus the HF metadata keys a default
554	    instance emits via `to_dict()` (so serialized configs still round-trip).
555	
556	    Args:
557	        model_dict: The merged `model` subtree about to construct the HF config.
558	        model_config_cls: The `OplmConfig` (HF `PretrainedConfig`) class.
559	
560	    Raises:
561	        ValueError: If `model_dict` contains any key outside the allowed set.
562	    """
563	    params = inspect.signature(model_config_cls.__init__).parameters
564	    allowed = {
565	        name
566	        for name, p in params.items()
567	        if name != "self" and p.kind not in (p.VAR_KEYWORD, p.VAR_POSITIONAL)
568	    }
569	    # HF metadata keys (model_type, transformers_version, architectures, dtype,
570	    # id2label, ...) are not constructor params but round-trip through a
571	    # serialized config; a default instance enumerates exactly that set.
572	    allowed |= set(model_config_cls().to_dict())
573	
574	    unknown = sorted(set(model_dict) - allowed)
575	    if unknown:
576	        raise ValueError(
577	            f"Unknown model config key(s): {unknown}. Check for typos "
578	            "(e.g. 'canon_enabled', not 'cannon_enabled'); valid keys come from "
579	            "OplmConfig.__init__ and HuggingFace PretrainedConfig metadata."
580	        )
581	
582	
583	def load_config(argv: list[str]) -> OplmConfig:
584	    """Load config from defaults, optional preset, optional YAML file, and CLI overrides.
585	
586	    Merge order (later overrides earlier): defaults → preset → YAML file → CLI overrides.
587	
588	    Args:
589	        argv: Command-line arguments (e.g. sys.argv[1:]).
590	            Supports ``--preset <name>`` for size presets, ``--config <path>``
591	            for YAML files, ``--name <run>`` for the W&B run name, and dotlist
592	            overrides like ``model.num_hidden_layers=32``.
593	
594	    Returns:
595	        Fully resolved and validated OplmConfig. If a YAML file was used,
596	        ``cfg.train.config_path`` is populated with its absolute path. ``--name``
597	        sets ``cfg.train.wandb_run_name`` unless that field was explicitly set in
598	        the YAML or via a CLI override (an explicit value always wins); when both
599	        are unset it stays ``None`` (W&B assigns a random name). ``--name`` also
600	        seeds ``cfg.train.output_dir`` to ``./<name>`` unless ``train.output_dir``
601	        was explicitly set in the YAML or via a CLI override.
602	    """
603	    base: DictConfig = OmegaConf.structured(OplmConfig)
604	
605	    # Disable struct mode to allow dynamic keys under data.train
606	    # (data.train can be a string path or a nested dict of datasets).
607	    OmegaConf.set_struct(base, False)
608	
609	    # Authoritative YAML defaults layer (model → train → data). These are the
610	    # human-editable home for defaults and override the dataclass fallbacks.
611	    for package, filename in _BASE_CONFIG_LAYERS:
612	        base = cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.merge(base, _load_packaged_yaml(package, filename)))
613	
614	    # Extract --config, --preset, and --name flags
615	    config_path: str | None = None
616	    preset: str | None = None
617	    run_name: str | None = None
618	    remaining: list[str] = []
619	    i = 0
620	    while i < len(argv):
621	        if argv[i] == "--config" and i + 1 < len(argv):
622	            config_path = str(Path(argv[i + 1]).expanduser().resolve())
623	            i += 2
624	        elif argv[i] == "--preset" and i + 1 < len(argv):
625	            preset = argv[i + 1]
626	            i += 2
627	        elif argv[i] == "--name" and i + 1 < len(argv):
628	            run_name = argv[i + 1]
629	            i += 2
630	        else:
631	            remaining.append(argv[i])
632	            i += 1
633	
634	    # Collect user overrides (preset → --config → CLI dotlist), applied on top
635	    # of the authoritative base layer.
636	    overrides: list[DictConfig] = []
637	    if preset is not None:
638	        overrides.append(get_preset_config(preset))
639	    if config_path is not None:
640	        overrides.append(cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.load(config_path)))
641	    if remaining:
642	        overrides.append(OmegaConf.from_dotlist(remaining))
643	
644	    override_dicts = [OmegaConf.to_container(ov, resolve=True) for ov in overrides]
645	    _reject_removed_sequence_length_alias(override_dicts)
646	
647	    # Whether the user explicitly set the W&B run name (YAML or CLI override).
648	    # An explicit value — even ``null`` — wins over the ``--name`` flag below.
649	    user_set_run_name = any(
650	        _lookup_nested_mapping_value(ov, ("train", "wandb_run_name")) is not _NESTED_VALUE_MISSING
651	        for ov in override_dicts
652	    )
653	
654	    # Whether the user explicitly set the output directory (YAML or CLI override).
655	    # An explicit value wins over the ``--name``-derived default below.
656	    user_set_output_dir = any(
657	        _lookup_nested_mapping_value(ov, ("train", "output_dir")) is not _NESTED_VALUE_MISSING
658	        for ov in override_dicts
659	    )
660	
661	    # Merge all overrides into base
662	    for ov in overrides:
663	        base = cast("DictConfig", OmegaConf.merge(base, ov))
664	
665	    # Build train/data dataclasses (triggers their __post_init__ validation);
666	    # `model` is an Any field so it round-trips as a plain dict here.
667	    cfg: OplmConfig = OmegaConf.to_object(base)  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]  # OmegaConf union
668	
669	    # Instantiate the HF model config from the merged `model` subtree. HF owns
670	    # derivation (head_dim, intermediate_size, rope_dim/nope_dim) and validation.
671	    # Derived fields are omitted unless set, resolving to None → derived inside
672	    # OplmModelConfig.__init__. Unknown / mistyped `model.*` keys are rejected
673	    # here (run-config path) rather than silently absorbed into
674	    # PretrainedConfig **kwargs; from_pretrained() stays permissive for
675	    # checkpoint compatibility.
676	    from oplm.model import OplmConfig as OplmModelConfig
677	
678	    model_dict = cast("dict[str, Any]", OmegaConf.to_container(base.model, resolve=True) or {})
679	    _reject_unknown_model_keys(model_dict, OplmModelConfig)
680	    cfg.model = OplmModelConfig(**model_dict)
681	
682	    # Cross-config divisibility check: pad_to_multiple_of must evenly divide
683	    # max_position_embeddings so padded lengths can never overflow position IDs.
684	    # This is the only place both cfg.data and the resolved cfg.model are available.
685	    if cfg.data.pad_to_multiple_of is not None:
686	        max_pos = cfg.model.max_position_embeddings
687	        ptm = cfg.data.pad_to_multiple_of
688	        if max_pos % ptm != 0:
689	            raise ValueError(
690	                f"pad_to_multiple_of ({ptm}) must evenly divide "
691	                f"model.max_position_embeddings ({max_pos}); "
692	                f"{max_pos} % {ptm} = {max_pos % ptm}"
693	            )
694	
695	    # Cross-section compatibility (train.parallelism vs data.eval); also re-checked at
696	    # Trainer.__init__ for configs built without load_config.
697	    validate_parallelism_compat(cfg)
698	
699	    cfg.train.config_path = config_path
700	
701	    # Propagate --name to the W&B run name unless explicitly set in YAML/CLI.
702	    if run_name is not None and not user_set_run_name:
703	        cfg.train.wandb_run_name = run_name
704	
705	    # Propagate --name to the output directory (./<name>) unless explicitly set.
706	    if run_name is not None and not user_set_output_dir:
707	        cfg.train.output_dir = run_name
708	
709	    return cfg
710	
711	
712	def serialize_config(cfg: OplmConfig) -> str:
713	    """Serialize a resolved :class:`OplmConfig` to reloadable YAML text.
714	
715	    The ``model`` subtree is an HF ``OplmConfig`` (serialized via ``to_dict``);
716	    ``train`` and ``data`` are dataclasses. The result round-trips through
717	    ``load_config(["--config", <path>])``. Shared by the top-level run config dump
718	    and the per-checkpoint ``config.yaml``.
719	    """
720	    from dataclasses import asdict
721	
722	    model_dict = cfg.model.to_dict()
723	    # `auto_map` is HF `register_for_auto_class`/`save_pretrained` plumbing for
724	    # trust_remote_code loading (see oplm/__init__.py's registration calls), not
725	    # something a user ever sets. `PretrainedConfig.register_for_auto_class` stamps
726	    # it onto the config instance *in place* the first time any `save_pretrained`
727	    # call runs against it -- e.g. this very checkpoint's own `hf/` export just
728	    # below in `save_checkpoint`, or an earlier checkpoint's, since `cfg.model` is
729	    # one shared, mutable object across every checkpoint in a run. Once stamped, it
730	    # sticks for the rest of the process, so every checkpoint after the first one
731	    # saved would otherwise carry it into config.yaml -- and fail to round-trip
732	    # through `load_config` (`_reject_unknown_model_keys` rejects it: a freshly
733	    # constructed default instance's own `to_dict()` never has it either, since it
734	    # is only ever added by `save_pretrained`, not by construction).
735	    model_dict.pop("auto_map", None)
736	
737	    config_dict = {
738	        "model": model_dict,
739	        "train": asdict(cfg.train),
740	        "data": asdict(cfg.data),
741	    }
742	    return OmegaConf.to_yaml(OmegaConf.create(config_dict))
743
